newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Chubais sets out economic priorities.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chubais sets out economic priorities.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, a pro-market liberal, set out his government's economic priorities on Tuesday but said the state should have a larger role in regulating the market economy.

"We are for strengthening the role of the state, for reestablishing it where it was lost, but we have to act wisely to reach this target," Chubais told the Federation Council upper house of parliament.

Chief reformer Chubais, in charge of the government while Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is on vacation, told the Federation Council that the government had to cut spending and boost revenue to ensure 1997 budget targets could be met.
Tight parameters for the 1998 budget had already been drawn up and Chubais said the plans had to be "realistic". Subsidies and tax breaks should be scrapped, he said.
Chubais presented a seven-point list which summarised government policy statements over the last few weeks and months. It comprised the following:
**Sequestration -- cutting spending levels across the board in order to offset a dismal shortfall in tax revenues
**Drawing up and approving a realistic 1998 budget
**Approval of the tax code. The document, which has already been submitted to the State Duma lower house of parliament, will underpin the 1998 budget
**Lowering tariffs for so-called natural monopolies -- including gas, electricity and transport
**Communal reform, including the reduction of expensive across-the-board housing subsidies in order to ease pressure on local budgets.

The lower house is due to discuss the government's sequestration plan on Wednesday, and Chubais urged deputies to approve the first reading of the new tax code before the summer recess starts on June 21.
The new code aims to make Russia's convoluted tax system more workable and transparent.

Chubais said a series of extraordinary measures would bring some 34 trillion roubles of additional budget revenues, mostly from Russia's major tax debtors such as Gazprom GAZP.RTS gas monopoly, carmaker AvtoVaz AVST.RTS and Sibneft and Nizhnevartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS oil firms.
